newsitem.title: UK: Export data supportive for palm oil - Europe trade.
newsitem.headline: Export data supportive for palm oil - Europe trade.

text.p: Data released by Malaysian cargo surveyor General de Surveillance (SGS) on Monday morning was seen as supportive for palm oil, European vegetable oil traders said.
SGS put local exports during May at 672,805 tonnes, above trade expectations of 630,000 to 650,000 tonnes.
Earlier cargo surveyor Caleb Bert had estimated exports at 641,950 tonnes.
However, European traders were puzzled by the reaction of the Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange (KLCE).
"The data looks supportive and traders in Asia seemed bullish in there outlook, but the KLCE has come down, which is puzzling people over here," said one.
One possible cause of the downturn in Malaysian could be rising production.
"Palm oil is coming into its peak production months and there is still no sign of any buying by India, Pakistan or China," said another trader.
In early trading on Monday morning crude palm oil cif Europe fetched $550 a tonne for June with further offers across the board at $552.50, $2.50 to $5 above Friday's close, with buyers at $547.50.
Chicago is expected to dominate the soft oils with soybean prices rising on concern over supplies and higher weekly crush data.
However, although prices in Europe are expected to follow the trend in Chicago, they will not mark the U.S. market too closely.
"U.S. soy bean traders are concerned about stocks but 90 percent of soybeans coming into Europe come from South America so we foresee no problems," said one trader.
But even in Chicago soy oil is the weakest market with lacklustre USDA weekly export sales and above market expectation crush figures weighing on the market.
Coconut oil prices are seen as consolidating after recent volatile trading.
"The shorts have been taken out and the next stage should see people go long in the forward positions in anticipation of higher prices later in the year," said one trader.
